Training/eval data is fetched from a public GitHub raw URL (a static, pre-generated corpus), not the closed API originally used to generate it.

vram_basis: No torch_dtype is specified anywhere in the codebase (AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(...).to(device) with no dtype arg), which loads Llama-3-8B-Instruct in fp32 by default: ~32GB of weights alone, exceeding 24GB. Switching to bf16 (a one-line fix, since only a soft concept-embedding is trained and the 8B model stays frozen) would bring this to roughly 18-22GB including backprop activations.
est_runtime_basis: No compute stated; batch_size=20, epochs=5, with sentence-activation caching (CachedDataset) to avoid repeated full-model forward passes.
headline_artifact: trainings_logs.plot_final_token_accuracy / plot_top_tokens outputs from each experiments/*.py script (one script per concept: animals.py, chinese.py, numbers.py, mammals.py, mammals_words.py, palindromes.py), showing convergence (or failure) to the target single-token label
blockers: As coded, loads an 8B model in fp32 (~32GB) which does not fit a 24GB 3090 without a manual bf16/fp16 edit

No single unified entrypoint -- each concept/claim (animal, Chinese, number, mammal balanced/unbalanced, palindrome) is a separate standalone script

CLI docstrings also show 'anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet' as an example judge/generator model, but the artifacts actually checked into the repo used the open-weight gpt-oss-120b judge instead.

models_needed.hf_id: custom dense Transformer (GRAM/LoRA/DEMix/filtering/MaxEnt), trained from scratch, 26M-2B+ params per src/run/experiment/scaling/realistic/base/run_all.py (README states up to 5B for the full paper)

vram_basis: Scaling experiment trains dense Transformers from scratch at 50M/100M/200M/400M/800M/2000M(+5B per README) params x 3 seeds x 5 methods, using DDP (no parameter sharding) across 8 GPUs by default. Even at the 800M-2B scales, Adam optimizer state (fp32, 2x params) plus fp32 master weights plus bf16 weights/grads exceeds 24GB per replica once you add activation memory; the 5B scale is far beyond a single 3090 under this training setup regardless.
est_runtime_basis: Compute-optimal (Chinchilla-style) token budgets scale with each of 6-7 model sizes up to 2-5B params, x 3 seeds x 5 methods (baseline/GRAM/LoRA/DEMix/filtering) plus MaxEnt unlearning and adversarial-elicitation fine-tuning passes; the authors ran this on a 24-32-node 8xH200 Slurm/RunPod cluster, i.e. hundreds of GPU-days, not something a single 3090 completes in any practical timeframe even ignoring the VRAM ceiling.
headline_artifact: analysis/scaling/plot.py (Fig. 7: Compute Ratio vs. params, GRAM/LoRA/filtering/MaxEnt across 50M-5B) and analysis/partial/plot_full.py (Fig. 6: 50%-labeled partial setting)
blockers: Default/documented training setup is 8x GPU DDP (torchrun --nproc_per_node=8); no single-GPU config is provided for the scaling or partial-labeling experiments
Model scales relevant to the headline claim (400M-5B) do not fit a single 24GB card even with mixed precision, given DDP replicates full optimizer state per device rather than sharding it
Actual paper runs used a 24-32-node 8xH200 RunPod/Slurm cluster (documented in src/run/experiment/slurm.md) -- multiple orders of magnitude beyond a solo 3090 budget

No packaged dependency manifest (README explicitly: 'There is no packaged manifest'); HF_TOKEN required for the tokenized datasets, and results/ upload uses an S3 bucket (ae-gradient-routing-results) by default
Checkpoints are git-ignored and not published, so even partial reruns can't warm-start from the authors' trained models
notes: The core mechanism (GRAM module ablation vs. baseline/LoRA/DEMix/filtering) is demonstrated at a tiny 26M scale in src/run/experiment/stories/, which is single-GPU-feasible and would test capability isolation and basic robustness, but not the compute-ratio-tracks-filtering scaling claim across 50M-5B or the realistic dual-use-domain (virology/cyber/nuclear) results the post's headline actually cites. Fidelity to the stated 50M-5B claim requires multi-node multi-GPU training explicitly documented as an 8xH200 cluster job.
